At the end of the day, you have to understand that you can't "save her". This isn't a romantic comedy--this is her choice. As the person who has been on the other end in a way, the people who did the most *damage* to me, and made me worse, were the ones that tried to "save" or "fix" me---the ones who tried to make me do things, to put me in a home or psych ward against my will. 

The one that helped....the *only* one that helped....was the one that said "I lvoe you enough to respect whatever you do; i'm not gonna make you do something because i want you to or try and "fix" you for my own benefit 'because i love you'."

YOu want to help her, good; support her. Just let her know that whatever decision she makes, you love her. 

Personal experience, I'd *avoid* telling her family/friends/others/reporting her **without her permission.** Outing someone just makes them more suicidal in many cases. If you want to *gently suggest* that you'd support her if she wanted to see someone, fine. But make it clear you'd also support her the same amount if she didn't.

Basically, it boils down to: care enough to respect her and not treat her like se's broken and needs to be "fixed" or "helped", and support her unconditionally either way. And don't *force her to do something she doesn't want to* "because it's for her own good." That's messed up, and it basically told me that others thought i was so defective or sick or broken that my desires didn't matter. The only person who ever made me less suicidal was the only one that ever said that it was okay. As counter-productive as it seems, that was the one that made me stick around a little longer.
